n: A companion to Psalm 127: everyone who reveres the Lord and walks in his ways is blessed — the blessing reaches into ordinary home life.

f.w: Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD

n: You will enjoy the fruits of your own work — a blessing, since invaders or famine often robbed farmers of their harvest.

f.w: thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands

n: The wife is like a fruitful grapevine in the inner rooms of the home; children are like young olive shoots around the table — full of promise and future fruit.

f.g: Young olive shoots that grow up around the parent tree.

n: This is how the one who reverences the Lord will be blessed.

f.g: Look! — calling attention to the point.

n: The blessing now comes from the temple in Zion. May you see Jerusalem prosper your whole life long.

f.w: The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion

n: May you live to see your grandchildren, and may peace rest on Israel. Personal blessing and community blessing go together.
